- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.1) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.1) and price is rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overcorrects downward; delay downward adjustment until 2–3 days after peak.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.1), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after rising), model often fails to recognize it; add 1–2% downward bias in next 5–7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window; apply 0.5–1.5% downward correction for first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +0.2), model often fails to account for exhaustion; reduce forecast by 1–3% after 5th day.
